text:
anya: Quick PSA — console 'tombstone' badge for v1 looks fine, but noticed routing still honors sticky v1 tokens for 24h after tombstone which sometimes triggers fallback to v2 mid-request. That fallback is causing duplicate quota attribution in billing telemetry. Anyone else see this?

ben: Saw it in prod traces yesterday. Fallback path sets header `X-Route-Fallback` then a downstream proxy re-credits quota. :grimacing:

maria: Is this a console-only UX change or a routing layer mismatch?

sam: Likely routing mismatch. Console flips the tenant flag with TTL=24h and runtime only checks the flag at request start; fallback constructs a new internal request with a different auth token and we increment quota again. Short fix: ensure fallback reuses original token/id if possible.

josh-ux: From UX side, users expect tombstone->immediate unpin in console. If backend sticky behavior persists we should show a 'compatibility window' tooltip instead of a hard banner.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deploy completed: routing-service v3.44.2 rolled to canary @ 1747203300

anya: We need a short-term mitigation + a long-term change. Short-term: dedupe billing events on request id or header. Long-term: change tombstone flow to unpin affinity immediately when the admin selects that option.

ben: Dedupe via `X-Orig-Request-Id` header looks easiest. Billing pipeline can ignore duplicate events with same orig id + tenant. Also add a metric `fallback_quota_dup` for visibility.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR to: (a) add `X-Orig-Request-Id` propagation on fallback, (b) add dedupe in billing side, (c) dashboard tile + alert. Also propose console change: allow admins to choose `immediate_unpin` vs `graceful_unpin` per rollout.

maria: For rollout UX, we should add a canary slider that routes N% new traffic to v2 while leaving pinned tokens alone until they expire. Console could show an estimated quota delta for the tenant when switching modes.

josh-ux: I'll mock a compact badge: "Graceful (pinned tokens route to v1 for 24h)" with a link to change to "Immediate unpin". Need concise copy for security/compliance review.

qa-robot: repro steps: 1) set tenant pin=true; 2) tombstone via console; 3) send concurrent requests; 4) observe billing logs. Sample command: ```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer T-abc' https://api.redwood.ai/generate```

anya: Thanks. Sam — can you also add a per-tenant alert if `fallback_quota_dup` > 5/min? That will help catch regressions during rollout.

sam: Yes. PR later today, alert with 1m evaluation window and a runbook link.

deploy-bot: Note: canary v3.44.2 ships with fallback dedupe OFF by default behind feature-flag `routing.dedupe_on_fallback`. Toggle available in console flags panel.

ben: Action items recap: (1) Sam: PR for header propagation + billing dedupe + alert, (2) Josh: UX mock + compact badge + copy, (3) Maria: spec for canary slider + quota estimator, (4) Ops: suppress telemetry noise and monitor `fallback_quota_dup`.

anya: Assigning owners in GH: sam -> r/infra, josh-ux -> r/console-ux, maria -> r/product-console, ben -> r/observability. Quick sync 11:30 in #eng-platform.

maria: One more note — product wants the console to warn if a tenant has active long-lived tokens before letting immediate unpin. Could add a preflight check that lists stale pins.

josh-ux: Good call. I'll add a small preflight modal that shows count of pinned tokens by age + a confirm checkbox.

ben: Also let's log a structured event `tombstone_unpin_user_action` when admin toggles immediate_unpin so billing/analytics can reconcile.

anya: Great. If no objections I'll start an RFC draft summarizing the mitigation + UX changes and link PRs there.

sam: No objections. Thanks everyone.
